candidates.rationale: dc1e16e4b07f7b9d is a crossover of two near-siblings still visible in the archive: 5dd286d81a38617b (TS_MEAN(range/open,63), mean_ic 0.0113, essentially all of the parent's fit-window IC on its own) and the now-evicted 85803c2daa426146 (TS_MEAN(range/dollar_volume,10), mean_ic 0.0063, well under 80% alone). Because the parent is still a live archive member, keeping either branch verbatim (even at a new window) is not available: each branch is itself a >=4 node complete subtree of the parent, and a bare window bump on the same field/aggregator is a documented dead end here (TS_MEAN($open|$dollar_volume, W) restates the same cross-sectional price/liquidity level regardless of W, so it either matches the parent's own branch outright or clears archive_subtree only to fail correlation against it). The open-normalized leg carries essentially all the fit-window IC, but every open-anchored or close-anchored replacement for it collapses onto the still-live grandparent or the archive's documented close-family saturation (TS_STD($close) is explicitly noted dead at w=5/10/21/63 in this run). So this drops that leg entirely and keeps the dollar-volume side, but swaps its normalizer from a smoothed level (TS_MEAN) to its own 21-day dispersion (TS_STD): 'is today's range large relative to how erratic recent trading value has been' instead of 'relative to its typical level', a different aggregator entirely rather than a window edit of either live sibling. This is the best-supported simplification available, not a verified one: no live member uses TS_STD($dollar_volume,*) in this role, so it clears archive_subtree by construction, but its fit-window IC relative to the parent's 0.0112 could not be measured directly (this session's sandbox blocks executing the scoring harness), so the 80% retention bar is a real, unverified risk here.

candidates.changed_node: the guarded ($close - $low) / ($close + 1e-8) same-day recovery-off-the-low ratio, replaced with TS_RANK($close, 21)
candidates.rationale: 23746d2508bcf88d already has two live mutation children that validate swapping its second leg: cf8910d8f4106571 replaced the (close-low)/close ratio with TS_DELTA(close,3)/close and kept 88.6% of parent IC (0.0169 vs 0.0191) while dropping to 2 fields, and 04b1950db0d43981 kept $low but added a TS_RANK(...,21) wrapper. Both are already archive members, so neither can be resubmitted, and their own rationale documents that any same-day OHLC-anchor swap on the untouched ratio stays rho>=0.85 with the parent, and that any monotonic transform of bare $close collapses onto the separate earnings-yield family (5da2da3341879251, RANK(eps/close)) at rho 0.886-0.998, per that lineage's own recorded rejections. This candidate avoids both traps at once: it drops $low and the epsilon-guarded division outright (no field-level ratio survives to restate cf8910d8 or 04b1950db, and no monotonic close transform survives to restate 5da2da), replacing the same-day 'close position above today's low, scaled by close' with TS_RANK($close, 21), the stock's own trailing 21-day close percentile. That keeps the core idea (is price sitting near a recent high or low) but moves it to a rolling, self-relative, already-bounded measure, so the epsilon guard is no longer needed at all. No live archive member wraps bare $close in TS_RANK (checked directly against the run archive), so this is structurally distinct from the whole eps/close family as well as from both of the parent's own children. IC retention could not be verified against the real panel in this session (harness execution was unavailable), so this is the best-reasoned candidate rather than a confirmed one.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.

Return exactly one simplification per parent, 2 in total.
